Ticket #07 — Ticket Seat Holds

Difficulty: Medium

Context

You maintain temporary seat reservations for event checkout. A hold gives one buyer a short opportunity to purchase one seat. Confirmation turns an unexpired hold into a booking; a confirmed seat must remain unavailable after the original hold deadline.

Practice report

At 12:00 on 2030-01-01, hold A1 for buyer-a under h1, using the default five-minute lifetime. At exactly 12:05, call hold("A1", "buyer-b", "h2").

Observation Current starter Expected
New hold result False True
Owner stored for seat A1 buyer-a buyer-b

Use the injected clock to reproduce this without sleeping.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A seat has at most one live hold or confirmed booking. Before expiry, a competing buyer cannot take the seat.
  • An unconfirmed hold expires at its deadline: it must stop blocking a new buyer at that instant and afterward.
  • A live hold ID cannot be reused to claim a second seat. Rejected requests preserve existing seat and hold ownership.
  • Only the owning buyer can confirm an unexpired, unconfirmed hold.
  • Confirmation keeps the seat unavailable permanently for this exercise; passing the temporary hold deadline does not release a confirmed booking.
  • Unknown seats, missing buyer/hold IDs, and unavailable confirmations fail without replacing an existing booking.

Out of Scope

Keep the supplied seats and clock. Payments, booking cancellation, seat maps, and multiple-process locking are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Trace holding and confirmation around the deadline. Add tests immediately before and exactly at expiry, a competing buyer, hold-ID reuse, and confirmation by the wrong buyer. Assert the stored owner, not just the returned boolean.
